source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Digoxin is eliminated mainly by hepatic metabolism, so renal impairment has little effect on exposure or toxicity.","B":"Digoxin dosing generally increases with age and renal impairment because reduced kidney function accelerates clearance.","C":"Digoxin is substantially renally eliminated, so impaired kidney function can prolong exposure and increase toxicity.","D":"Digoxin is removed only through the lungs, so kidney function does not influence dosing or monitoring requirements."}}
source_row.rationale: Digoxin is substantially eliminated by the kidneys, so renal impairment can prolong its half-life and increase exposure; maintenance dosing must account for renal function, age, body size and clinical response.
source_row.source_detail: Clinical pharmacology/specific populations: digoxin is primarily excreted by the kidneys; clearance correlates with creatinine clearance, and impaired renal function requires smaller maintenance doses and longer time to steady state. DailyMed digoxin labeling updated January 13, 2026; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: Why does mild renal impairment matter when an older adult is prescribed digoxin?
